a2a.note: An A2A Agent Card names the agent and where to reach it: a top-level url on a 0.3 card, or url, protocolBinding, and protocolVersion inside supportedInterfaces on a 1.0 card.

ucp.note: A UCP profile is a JSON document declaring supported capabilities; presence of JSON at the path is the signal.

llms-txt.note: llms.txt must begin with an H1 line.

agents-md.note: AGENTS.md has no required fields; a non-empty document at the site root is the signal.

aipref-content-usage-attachment.note: A Content-Usage line in robots.txt attaches AIPREF preferences to the site.

aipref-vocabulary.note: Vocabulary tokens are not validated; a non-empty Content-Usage value is the signal.

tdmrep.note: A TDMRep file carries tdm-reservation or tdm-policy fields.

cloudflare-content-signals-policy.note: Content Signals are Content-Signal lines in robots.txt.

webbotauth.note: A signature directory is a JWKS served with its own media type.

web-bot-auth-signature-agent-card.note: The Signature Agent Card adds OAuth client registration fields to the directory.

ard.note: An ARD manifest is JSON with a top-level entries array.

ai-catalog-well-known-file.note: Deprecated predecessor path of the ARD manifest, still probed so the census can count migration.

aid.note: The AID well-known document mirrors the DNS TXT record, including uri.

adp.note: An ADP agent.json has identity and endpoints blocks.

ardp.note: ARDP meta declares TTL bounds and auth profiles.

ads.note: An Agent Directory Service lists catalog entries as JSON at /v1/agents.

adcp.note: adagents.json lists the publisher's authorised ad agents.

anp.note: ANP active discovery is a JSON-LD collection of AgentDescription items.

agora-protocol.note: Agora agents declare supported protocols as a JSON map at /.wellknown (sic).

api-catalog-rfc9727.note: RFC 9727 requires application/linkset+json with a linkset array.

rsl.note: RSL is referenced from robots.txt by a License line or an rsl.xml link.

agent-permissions-json.note: agent-permissions.json requires metadata and strict at top level.

auth-md.note: auth.md describes one or more of the three named flows.

ai-crawler-tokens-robots.note: A robots.txt group naming a known AI crawler token.

agents-json.note: agents.json extends OpenAPI with a flows field.

agents-txt.note: Competing agents.txt grammars share only the path; a non-empty file is the signal.

ai-txt.note: ai.txt carries Training, Scraping, Indexing or Caching directives.

lmos.note: An LMOS Thing Description references the LMOS namespace.

erc-8004.note: ERC-8004 agents publish a registration file at the domain they claim.

vi.note: A merchant publishes its Verifiable Intent document at a fixed well-known path.

oauth-metadata-for-agents.note: RFC 9728 protected resource metadata requires the resource field.

mcp.note: MCP endpoints are not at a fixed well-known path. On 2026-07-28, capabilities are read with server/discover; initialize is the legacy handshake for 2025-11-25 and earlier. The server card is GET <endpoint>/server-card.

agent-communication-protocol.note: IBM ACP was archived and merged into A2A; /agents is not expected on new deployments.

agentic-commerce-protocol.note: The probe is POST /checkout_sessions, which creates a checkout on the merchant; never run unauthenticated.

x402.note: A 402 challenge appears only on a URL that charges; there is no fixed path to check.

l402.note: L402 challenges appear only on paid URLs.

mpp.note: MPP challenges appear only on paid URLs.

s402.note: s402 challenges appear only on paid URLs.

nlweb.note: The probe is POST /ask with a question body; not run from a public tool.

agent-protocol-aief.note: The probe is POST /ap/v1/agent/tasks, which starts a task.

aitp.note: The probe is POST /threads, which creates a thread.

coral-protocol.note: The probe is POST /api/v1/local/session, which opens a session.

okf.note: Google Open Knowledge Format (OKF v0.2) web bundle index at /okf/index.md declaring okf_version.

vercel-agent-readability.note: A checklist, not a manifest; the llms-txt, agents-md, robots and sitemap checks cover its site-level items.

daap.note: DAAP rides on OAuth authorization server metadata; presence of that metadata does not prove the profile.

aap.note: AAP is a claims profile inside OAuth tokens; nothing at a fixed path proves it.

aauth.note: The Agent Authorization Grant is observed only inside a token request.

ap2.note: AP2 mandates are exchanged inside an authorised checkout; nothing is published at a fixed path.

ap2-checkout-mandate.note: A component of AP2, observable only inside a checkout.

vcap.note: VCAP credentials are presented during a payment, not published.

tap.note: Trusted Agent Protocol keys are fetched from the key service by keyID during a transaction.

agent-attribution-protocol.note: The probe is a vendor API call that needs an API key.

agent-audit-trail.note: Audit logs are exported from an operator-defined endpoint behind authentication.

artf.note: ARTF containers run inside the host platform; the health endpoint is internal.

erc-8183.note: An Ethereum contract; observable via eth_call, not HTTP.

erc-8226.note: An Ethereum contract; observable via eth_call, not HTTP.

dns-aid.note: DNS SVCB records; the HTTP well-known form is covered by the aid rule.

agtp.note: AGTP is its own application-layer protocol over QUIC or TCP.

slim.note: SLIM is a transport operated by data-plane nodes on its own wire protocol.

spiffe.note: SPIFFE identities are issued over a local socket, not published on the web.

wimse.note: WIMSE is an architecture for workload identity with no origin artefact.

http-message-signatures.note: Signatures appear on individual messages; the webbotauth directory rule covers the published key side.

ans.note: The ANS draft defines no fixed well-known path or record type.

aip.note: AIP is a client-side identity protocol with no origin artefact.

webmcp.note: WebMCP is a browser API on the page; observable only by executing the page.

web-agent-protocol.note: WAP records and replays browser actions; nothing is served by the site.

agent-client-protocol.note: ACP runs between an editor and a local agent binary over stdio.

anthropic-agent-skills-format.note: Agent Skills Discovery RFC v0.2.0 publishes a JSON skill index with a top-level skills[] array at /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json.

a2ui.note: A2UI is carried inside an AG-UI, A2A or MCP session; no fixed path.

ag-ui.note: The AG-UI run endpoint is application-defined.

mcp-apps.note: MCP Apps are declared inside an MCP server's tools/list; find the server first.

openai-apps-sdk-manifests.note: Plugin manifests are registered with OpenAI, reached through the app's MCP endpoint.

oasf.note: OASF schemas live on the schema host, not on the origin using them.

aamp.note: AAMP registries are operated by IAB Tech Lab, not by the origin.

agora-commerce-protocol.note: Agora Commerce publishes at api.agoraproto.org, not on member origins.

osi.note: OSI is a schema for semantic models exchanged between tools, not an origin artefact.

nlip.note: NLIP is a message envelope between agents; ECMA-430 defines no discovery artefact at an origin.

emv-agentic-payments.note: A framework document for card-network payment specifications; nothing is published at an origin.

identity-assertion-authz-grant.note: draft-ietf-oauth-identity-assertion-authz-grant advertises the id-jag profile in authorization server metadata; the key alone shows the server publishes grant profiles, so check for urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-profile:id-jag in the value.

aiagent-auth.note: An IETF framework draft composing WIMSE, SPIFFE and OAuth flows; it defines no artefact of its own at an origin.

dan.note: DNS records of types AIINDEX (65502) at _agents.<domain> and AIDISCA (65501); not reachable by HTTP GET.

mcp-server-cards.note: SEP-2127 reserves GET <streamable-http-url>/server-card as application/mcp-server-card+json. That URL is not one well-known path on the origin; discovery is /.well-known/ai-catalog.json.

gbz-185-agent-interconnection.note: probe rule pending: Part 5 (discovery) full text not yet read for a well-known path

amp-ant.note: AMP mandates and payment tokens are exchanged inside an authorised wallet flow; nothing is published at a fixed path.

x401.note: A PROOF-REQUEST header appears only on a resource that asks for proof; there is no fixed path to check.

kya-os.note: KYA-OS SPEC.md section 10: servers SHOULD expose /.well-known/mcp with serverDid and capabilities.

kyapay-token.note: KYAPay tokens are presented per request by the agent; nothing is published at a fixed path on the resource server.

oauth-cimd.note: RFC 8414 metadata advertises CIMD support with client_id_metadata_document_supported.

iab-comp.note: CoMP defines request and response objects, not a fixed path; supply discovery is out of scope.

agent-commerce-kit.note: ACK identity and payment objects are exchanged between parties; no fixed path is defined.

cloudflare-markdown-for-agents.note: Needs an Accept: text/markdown request header on any page; the probe rule format cannot set request headers.

otel-genai-semconv.note: Telemetry naming conventions inside an operator's tracing pipeline; no origin artefact.

erc-8001.note: An Ethereum contract; observable via eth_call, not HTTP.

erc-8126.note: An Ethereum contract; observable via eth_call, not HTTP.

erc-8196.note: An Ethereum contract; observable via eth_call, not HTTP.

erc-8444.note: A domain acknowledges an ERC-8444 controller address with value:controllers or value:controller in its ARD manifest.

jafar.note: The draft defines the JSON format only, not where the file is published.

anonymous-bot-auth.note: Anonymous credentials are presented per request; no site-side artefact is defined.

workload-authz-grant.note: The Workload Authorization Grant is a platform-signed JWT presented at a token endpoint; nothing is published at a fixed path.

oauth-id-continuation.note: The identity-continuation assertion is a token-exchange subject token; it is not published at a fixed path.

oauth-agent-delegation.note: Agent-Delegation is an HTTP header on a request signed with RFC 9421; there is no fixed path to fetch.

opena2a-aap.note: OpenA2A AAP is a token model. The named broker layer is not specified, and nothing is published at a fixed path.
